\[
M(c)=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{c^3(8-27c)}{32},&0<c\le \dfrac29,\\[6pt]
\dfrac1{1458},&\dfrac29\le c\le \dfrac12.
\end{cases}
\]

Let
\[
b=\min\left(c,\frac29\right),\qquad a=\frac b2 .
\]
The optimal paths use only slopes \(-1,0,1\), reach the positive height \(b\), and reach the negative height \(-a\).

For \(0<c<2/9\), so \(b=c,a=c/2\), the plateau lengths are
\[
P=\frac13-\frac{3c}{2},\qquad N=\frac23-\frac{3c}{2}.
\]
Up to time reversal, the unique optimal path is
\[
0 \xrightarrow[\text{slope }1]{c} c
\ \xrightarrow[\text{hold}]{P}\ c
\ \xrightarrow[\text{slope }-1]{3c/2}\ -\frac c2
\ \xrightarrow[\text{hold}]{N}\ -\frac c2
\ \xrightarrow[\text{slope }1]{c/2}\ 0.
\]
Equivalently, the control is
\[
u=1,0,-1,0,1
\]
on consecutive intervals of lengths
\[
c,\quad \frac13-\frac{3c}{2},\quad \frac{3c}{2},\quad \frac23-\frac{3c}{2},\quad \frac c2,
\]
or the time-reversed control. At \(c=2/9\), the same formula holds with \(P=0,N=1/3\).

For \(2/9<c\le1/2\), the cap is inactive. Up to time reversal, the unique optimal path is
\[
0\xrightarrow[\text{slope }1]{2/9}\frac29
\xrightarrow[\text{slope }-1]{1/3}-\frac19
\xrightarrow[\text{hold}]{1/3}-\frac19
\xrightarrow[\text{slope }1]{1/9}0.
\]

Proof sketch. For a path whose positive maximum is \(b\), rearrangement and convexity show that an optimizer must spend all positive plateau time at \(b\), all negative plateau time at some \(-a\), and use unit-speed ramps between them. Extra oscillations waste time and decrease the cubic integral. Thus every optimizer has, up to reversal, the trapezoidal form above.

For such a path the total transition time is \(2(a+b)\). If the plateau lengths at \(b\) and \(-a\) are \(P,N\), then
\[
P+N=1-2(a+b),
\]
and the zero-mean condition gives
\[
bP-aN+b^2-a^2=0.
\]
Solving,
\[
P=\frac{a-(a+b)^2}{a+b},\qquad
N=\frac{b-(a+b)^2}{a+b}.
\]
The cubic integral is
\[
J(a,b)=\frac{b^4-a^4}{2}+b^3P-a^3N
=(b-a)\left(ab-\frac{(a+b)^3}{2}\right).
\]
For fixed \(b\), this is maximized at \(a=b/2\), provided \(P,N\ge0\). That feasibility condition is
\[
\frac b2\ge \left(\frac{3b}{2}\right)^2,
\]
i.e.
\[
b\le \frac29.
\]
Hence if \(c\le2/9\), take \(b=c,a=c/2\), giving
\[
M(c)=\left(\frac c2\right)\left(\frac{c^2}{2}-\frac{27c^3}{16}\right)
=\frac{c^3(8-27c)}{32}.
\]
If \(c\ge2/9\), the best admissible positive height is \(b=2/9\), \(a=1/9\), yielding
\[
M(c)=\frac1{1458}.
\]
The equality conditions in the rearrangement force exactly the listed bang-bang controls, up to time reversal and equality almost everywhere.
